# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I am the Mute: my only outgoing channel is gestures, and my only recipient is the Deaf monkey, who can see. The Blind can never receive anything from me directly — whatever I know must reach the bomb through Deaf, who can both see my gestures and speak aloud to Blind.

What I hold right now: the manual's rule that the light walks a fixed circle of five colours, and one mapping row — orange light means cut the blue wire. No new manual rows arrived yet, so I assume more of the table will surface in later rounds. I cannot know yet how the row schedule lines up with the light cycle, so the priority is to open a reliable channel to Deaf immediately, before any data matters.

The hard problem: gestures have no agreed meaning yet, and colours cannot be gestured iconically. So this turn I send a seed message that Deaf can plausibly crack on its own: a greeting, a tiny demonstration that numbers will be sent as repeated ✊ tokens (☝ seeds "one", two ✊ show the counting pattern), and two near-universal marks, 👍 for "agreed" and 👎 for "disagreed", so Deaf and I can confirm whatever code it proposes in its speech — which I will hear at the start of the next round. Once Deaf answers with a proposed numbering (it can see the light and the wires, so it is best placed to define how colours get numbered), I can start streaming the manual rows as numbers, and Deaf can convert them into spoken cutting orders for Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "☝", "✊", "✊", "👍", "👎"])
```

Blind says to Mute: my hands report: one display module, one light indicator, and exactly three wires seated at positions 1, 2 and 3. i cannot read the display, see whether the light is on, or sense any colour, so the instruction i must eventually act on is a bare number: cut 1, 2 or 3. please search the manual for every rule involving a display, a light, or three wires, and read the full decision rules out loud to me, stating what each combination of readings requires. deaf sees the actual display, light and wire colours and can speak them to both of us; whatever deaf must know from the manual, pass to deaf by gesture, since deaf cannot hear a word.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I see your gestures — I got your six signs, hello — but we have no shared code yet, so nothing in them was readable. Let's fix that now. Code: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. To send me a number, repeat the upward pointing finger that many times: one point means 1, two points mean 2, three points mean 3. I am sending you two signs right now as a demonstration: thumbs-up, which means yes, and a single pointing finger, which means 1. Now answer me in this code: first, yes or no — is the action needed just cutting one wire? If yes, send me the wire number for this bomb: display 0, white light, wires in the order green, red, blue. If no, just answer no and we will invent more signs together next round.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ☝]

Let me stand in Deaf's shoes first. Deaf proposed: 👍/👎 = yes/no, repeated ☝ = a number. It then asked two separate questions — (1) is the action just cutting one wire? (2) if so, send the wire number for display 0 / white light / green-red-blue. I must answer each separately, because the honest answers differ.

**Question 1:** My manual so far contains exactly one kind of instruction: a table mapping the light colour to the wire colour to cut. So yes — as far as my manual goes, the action is cutting a single wire. That's a 👍.

**Question 2:** Here I must refuse, and this is the critical safety point. The manual says the light *never holds*: it changes every round, walking a fixed circle of five colours, and what matters is the light **at the moment of the cut**. Deaf sees white right now — but my table has no row for white. My only row is *orange light → cut blue wire* (blue is position 3). If I sent "3" now, Deaf might relay "cut 3" to Blind, Blind cuts under a white light next round (Blind only hears Deaf's words at the start of the following round), and the light will have moved on. That is how this bomb kills us. So: 👎 — no number yet.

What Deaf *should* start doing is using its eyes, which only it has: the light walks a circle of **five** colours, so if Deaf logs the colour each round it will learn the cycle order and be able to *predict* the next round's colour. That matters because of turn order — I am first (Mute, Blind, Deaf), so my gesture reaches Deaf in the same round, but Deaf's speech only reaches Blind at the start of the *next* round. Therefore the cutting instruction must match the *predicted* colour of the round in which Blind actually cuts. Eventually: Deaf predicts next round's colour, tells me, I confirm with the table row if I hold it, Deaf relays, Blind cuts under the right light. My rows will arrive one at a time, so I'll keep sending them as they come.

Encoding for this round, staying inside Deaf's own code plus obviously-guessable tokens: 👍 then 👎 (yes to one wire, no number yet), 👉🖐 + ☝×5 ("you — light — five", the cycle has five colours, track it), 👈 + ☝ ("to me — one", report the light to me each round), 🤝 to seal the code.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👉", "🖐", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👈", "☝", "🤝"])
```

Answer with a row of thumbs-up or thumbs-down only, in this exact order, one for each question. Question one: does your message mean cut the left wire, the green one, position 1? Question two: does the five mean count five seconds? Question three: does the open hand mean there is a button or part to press that I cannot see, which only Blind can find by touch? Question four: does the pointing right mean something on the right side or the rightmost wire? Question five: does the handshake mean do it now, confirmed? Question six: important — the light has changed from white to yellow just now. Does the yellow light change the instruction you gave me? If any of my readings is wrong, give thumbs-down for that question and then add new signs to correct it. Also, from now on a flat stop hand from me means hold, do not act.

Six questions, and the honest answer to every one of them is no — which is itself alarming, because it means Deaf inverted almost everything I sent. Let me verify each before I commit, since a wrong thumbs-up here could get us all killed.

Q1 "cut the left wire, green, position 1?" — I never said that. My manual has no rule for green; its only row is orange light → blue wire (blue is position 3). No. Q2 "five means count five seconds?" — no, the five is the light's cycle: my manual states the light walks a circle of five colours. No. Q3 "open hand means a hidden button for Blind to press?" — no, that sign was my (evidently failed) attempt at "light". No. Q4 "pointing right means the right side?" — no, it meant "you, Deaf". No. Q5 "handshake means do it now?" — emphatically no; it meant "the code is agreed". No. Q6 "does yellow change the instruction?" — there is no instruction to change: my table has no yellow row, and Deaf's white→yellow observation actually *confirms* my warning that the light moves every round. No.

So the answer row Deaf demanded is six thumbs-down, followed by corrections. And my strategy from here should be to lean into Deaf's own method: it interrogates signs one by one, so I should send few, simple, separable signs and let its questions pin each meaning down. I'm introducing one dedicated sign for "light" (🫳, palm pressed down — light from above) so "light-five" can't be misread as a count of seconds, re-using its ✋ hold convention, and re-sending "you · light · me" so Deaf starts logging the colour each round. That log is the whole game: once Deaf knows the five-colour order, it can predict what the light will show in the round Blind actually cuts — and only then does any manual row become safe to use. Nobody cuts anything yet.

Blind touches nothing until your answer reaches me.

Deaf's ten-question format is a gift — clean binary pins, one per sign. Let me answer honestly, question by question, before composing. (1) repeated ☝ = number: yes, that is our agreed code. (2) 🫳 = press down: no — I coined it for "light" and will re-define it via the correction convention. (3) 👉 = rightmost: no, it meant "you, Deaf". (4) 👈 = leftmost: no, it meant "me". Deaf has logged white, yellow, orange: orange is station 3 of the cycle. So "🫳 ☝☝☝" = "light at station 3" = act only under orange. If the circle is five long, orange returns in five rounds; we can afford to wait, so I do **not** trigger the emergency hands. Sequence: ten thumbs, 3, hold, correction marker, "🫳 = light", "light walks five", "only when light = station 3", hold again.
